_note: How the game LOOKS and FEELS: animation, hit effects, particles, UI motion and backgrounds. Nothing here changes the rules or balance. Times are in seconds, sizes in screen pixels unless they say tiles. Set a strength to 0 to switch an effect off.

characters._note: The animals. class_badge_radius: the class icon under each one, in pixels. shader_enabled false is the lighter option for slow phones (no shader at all; hits flash with a plain tint). shader_* values drive the per-animal shader (scripts/fx/unit.gdshader): a soft warm highlight on the edge facing the light (top-left), a soft cool rim light on the far edge (both edge_width texels wide at 56 pixels a tile, following the smooth edge so they stay smooth at any zoom), a little extra color punch, and gentle volume (gradient). The outline is the render's own single deep line; shader_line_tint above 0 tints it toward a dark shade (line_darkness) of the body color. In battle, team_outline_texels: a bold band in the team's color (blue yours, red the enemy's) round each sprite, this many texels wide (0: none; 3D models: "models" team_outline_px).

combat._note: Combat juice. A hit squashes the animal hit_squash and shoves it hit_knockback_pixels, adding up for hits close together but never past hit_squash_max and hit_knockback_max_pixels. Every hit shows when it lands: the attacker's wind-up plays first (started then if none was showing) and a shot flies (shot_tiles_per_second, between shot_min_seconds and shot_max_seconds), and only then do the flash, sparks, number and health-bar drop show; a defeat follows its last hit by defeat_after_hit_seconds. Each attack starts up to impact_jitter_seconds later than it could (0: armies strike in unison); a hit that comes within strike_grace_seconds of a strike lands on that strike. Health bars show once an animal is hurt and fade away (over health_bar_fade_seconds) when it hasn't been hit for health_bar_hide_after seconds. Strong hits (at least strong_hit_pct of the target's health, a charge, a pounce or a dive) flash, squash and knock back harder; only big hits (big_hit_pct) and knockouts pause the whole fight for a moment (hit-stop, at most once every hitstop_cooldown) and shake it. Shake is in pixels.

movement._note: How animals move on screen. Only the drawing: where an animal is in the fight never changes. It follows its place in the fight like a spring (follow_rate, higher = snappier; each animal's may differ by up to follow_variety, 0 in armies so ranks move as one), easing into and out of a run, and may wander up to march_wobble_tiles while marching (about every march_wobble_seconds; 0: armies march in step). Animals fighting are nudged apart on screen until their pictures are spread_body_share of their height apart (enemies in a scrap spread_enemy_share of that, a flier over an animal on the ground spread_air_share; one straight behind another also steps aside by spread_sideways, so a line staggers), at spread_rate, by at most spread_max_tiles, drifting back at spread_return_rate once there's room. They turn at turn_degrees_per_second toward where they walk or what they fight (a push never turns them), switch to the next of their 8 drawn directions only once turn_hysteresis_degrees past halfway, and pinch a little (turn_squash, for turn_squash_seconds) as they do. They walk only when moving on their own faster than walk_min_speed_tiles a second (for at least walk_hold_seconds); the walk plays as fast as the feet cover the ground (walk_stride_match 1 = exactly), kept between walk_min_fps and walk_max_fps. Stopping gives a small settling bounce (arrive_squash).

acting._note: How animals act, on top of their rendered animations. Each plays its idle and walk at its own pace (up to pace_variety faster or slower). It blinks (blink_seconds, every blink_every seconds) and, standing about with nothing in reach, fidgets now and then (fidget_every; the first after fidget_first). Faces drawn over the eyes: a squint on the wind-up, wide eyes for wide_seconds when hit, dizzy swirls when stunned or knocked out, drowsy lids when slowed, happy eyes when celebrating, a smug look for smug_seconds after a knockout. A hit makes it flinch (flinch_degrees) and bounce (hurt_bounce_pixels over hurt_seconds). Changing animation squashes it a little (transition_squash). Classes move their own way: wind-ups take windup_scale of the sheet's time (a Tank's big slow swing, a Tank Destroyer's quick one); Tanks plod (tank_hop of the walk's hop) with a thump and dust at each step (tank_step_squash); Tank Destroyers lean in (td_lean), crouch and spring at a pounce (td_pounce_pixels) and lunge further (td_lunge); Ranged kick back on every shot (ranged_recoil_pixels); fliers bob (air_bob_pixels at air_bob_speed), swoop (air_swoop_pixels), bank into turns (air_bank_degrees), rise before a dive (air_dive_rise_pixels) and drop into it (air_dive_drop_pixels). The winners celebrate for victory_seconds with bounces of victory_hop_pixels. A knockout poofs, or (defeat_fling_chance) bounces off the screen with a spin over defeat_fling_seconds. Stunned animals wobble (stun_wobble_degrees); slowed ones move at slow_pace with a Zzz every zzz_every seconds. Below sweat_below of their health they sweat (a drop every sweat_every seconds). Setting off, one may trip (trip_chance, for trip_seconds, at most once every trip_cooldown seconds). Specialist traits act too: a Stun animal's stunning blow comes after its rendered wind-up (a chest beat, a hiss, a roar) or, without one, a trembling stare stretching the wind-up by stun_windup_scale; a Slow animal's wind-up is a lazy yawn, slow_windup_scale as long, with drowsy eyes; a Splash animal rises splash_hop_pixels for a belly flop and lands squashed (splash_squash); a Burrow animal sinks into the ground over dig_seconds and pops out with a springy boing over emerge_seconds (emerge_hop_pixels high). Body plans walk their own way: fish wiggle (fish_wiggle_degrees), upright animals waddle (waddle_degrees), snakes ripple, frogs bound, seals and whales slide, shrimp scuttle.

choreography._note: How a fight is staged. It opens with a beat of intro_seconds: both herds hop into place (intro_hop_pixels high, spread over intro_hop_spread_seconds) and a bouncy FIGHT! banner (fight_banner_size) shows before the fight starts. When stall_animals or fewer are left and nobody has been knocked out for stall_after_seconds, the fight gradually plays faster, up to stall_max_speed after stall_ramp_seconds more (only how fast it plays, never what happens). The last knockout plays in slow motion (final_slow_motion) with a push-in (final_zoom, in over final_zoom_in_seconds, held until final_hold_seconds after the knockout, out over final_zoom_out_seconds); then the winners celebrate and the score shows.

effects._note: Particles. max_particles caps how many can be on screen at once (lower it on slow phones).

crowd._note: Keeping big fights readable and smooth. A fight is crowded from crowded_from_units animals on the field: bursts use particles_when_crowded of their particles, ordinary hits lose their claw and bite marks, fewer sparks and numbers show, and (plain_animals_when_crowded) the animals skip their shader so many of a kind draw together; that look is chosen as the herds come on, not mid-fight. Hit sparks: at most hit_sparks_max bursts at once (hit_sparks_when_crowded when crowded), each counting for spark_seconds; when that many are showing, a bigger hit takes the place of the smallest. Damage numbers work the same way (combat number_max_on_screen; numbers_when_crowded when crowded). Hit-stop pauses come at most once every hitstop_cooldown_when_crowded (a crowded fight has a knockout every moment).

models._note: The animals as real 3D models in battle (scripts/fx/model_stage.gd, art/models/battle/) instead of sprites. enabled: on everywhere: fights, the army while picking, the arena previews (off: the older sprites; Developer tools > Big army test (sprites) compares). render_scale_max: at most this many real pixels per layout pixel; msaa: antialiasing (0, 2 or 4); outline_px: the dark outline's width at one real pixel per layout pixel. In battle, a bold band in the team's color (blue yours, red the enemy's) team_outline_px wide sits outside the dark outline, so sides read at a glance even packed close (0: none); it's a second hull pushed team_outline_depth tiles back so the dark line stays on top. Shading is the 3D viewer's (viewer.json "look").

camera._note: The fight's camera. When the field grows for bigger herds (draft_rules.json "field"), the camera zooms out to it over about zoom_seconds. When the view already reaches the far fence (the line-up, a fight at the back), it eases on past it by up to scenery_back_tiles so the crowd behind the fence shows (data/arena_life.json); from scenery_reach_tiles away it doesn't.

celebrations._note: Big moments. After each fight the new score pops up over the field (score_pop_size) and flies into the score bar. A 3-star animal gets a slow-motion zoom (zoom in, hold, zoom out, with the field's animation slowed by star3_slow_motion), stars, confetti and a bouncy 3 STARS!, then keeps a gold glow (gold_glow) with a sparkle every gold_sparkle_seconds. Flawless: winning a round without losing an animal. Comeback Victory: winning the match after being 2 rounds down.

rivals._note: Rival Rangers. The VS screen before a match (versus_seconds before it goes on by itself, 0 to wait for a tap; it can't be tapped away before versus_min_seconds), and the rival's emote bubbles in the match (shown for emote_seconds, at most one every emote_gap_seconds). Beating a boss plays its celebration for boss_celebration_seconds before the result shows.

ui._note: Buttons and tappable cards squash when pressed and spring back with an overshoot (big panels squash less); popups and the Draft Duel panel pop in. Numbers in pills tick to their new value over count_seconds; short messages over the field stay for toast_seconds. A tap shows tap_sparkles sparkles; the main button on a screen breathes (breathe_amount, breathe_seconds); brass and gold icons catch a glint every glint_seconds; shop cards bob gently (card_bob_pixels, card_bob_seconds) and pop in stagger_seconds apart; a bought card flies to your herd (fly_seconds, along an arc fly_arc_pixels high) and lands with a squash (land_squash) and land_puffs puffs of dust.

pick._note: The Pick 3 screen. Card sizes are [width, height] in game pixels: offer_card for the options after round 1 (four animals in one tray, animal_tray, and two tools in another below it, tool_tray, each tray tray_padding pixels round its cards), start_card for round 1's collection grid, herd_card for your army row; choice_button for the Upgrade and +Squad buttons you get by tapping an animal in your army; army_height: how tall your army in formation is drawn while picking at least (it takes the room the options leave; framed with army_margin_tiles around it, at least army_min_tiles across, zoomed in up to army_max_zoom); slot_size for the three pick slots, undo_badge for the back arrow on your latest pick. Holding a card shows its info (see info). After a fight, the result shows for result_seconds before the next round's picks. The opponent takes between the two bot_pick_seconds over each pick.

bans._note: The ban screen before a match (scripts/ui/ban_screen.gd). card: [width, height] of each animal card in the grid (columns across). The coin flip spins for coin_seconds. The rival thinks for between the two think_seconds before each ban (dots bouncing by its face). A ban stamps a big red X on the card: it drops in over stamp_seconds from stamp_scale times its size, with a shake of stamp_shake pixels. After the last ban, the screen waits done_seconds and goes on to your deck.

transition._note: Changing screens: a leafy circle closes (cover_seconds) with a swirl of leaves, then opens on the next screen (reveal_seconds).

background._note: The arena behind the fight, in its full painted colors (arena_saturation 1 = as painted; the animals stand out by their dark outlines and bold colors), with gentle motion.

styles._note: How the animals' attack styles look (fx/style_look.gd on the animal, battle_field.gd for the moments; the rules are styles.json). The Brown Bear's swipe draws one wide arc across both targets for sweep_seconds. The Yeti glows frost the hit before its ground pound, which rings out in frost and shakes the field pound_shake. The turtle's shell is shell_width of its height across. A shot the Elephant takes for a teammate flashes a shield for shield_seconds. Colors for each. A Wild Boar's or Tiger's big first hit shakes the field slam_shake; Cerberus's three bites land bite_stagger_seconds apart. The Raccoon's trash flies lob_arc times higher and lob_flight times longer; the Cobra's shots take sniper_flight of the time, flat; the Camel's spit is spit_scale times as big; the Squirrel's pinecones are pellet_scale of a nut, pellet_stagger_seconds apart; the Orangutan's fruit bounces on bounce_seconds after it lands. Profile > Developer tools > Attack styles starts each animal's little fight over every showcase_seconds, its enemies biting at showcase_enemy_bite_pct; Slow plays it at showcase_slow_speed. The Falcon rises climb_pixels as it climbs away from a dive, stretched out with speed lines as it dives; the Owl leaves a ghostly owl_trail; the Harpy Eagle flies carry_lift of its height higher with its catch dangling below; a cracked animal shows a crack mark for as long as it lasts; the Condor grows feast_grow bigger for every fall it feasts on, a wisp flying into it over feast_seconds; the Dragon's burning line sweeps out over fire_reveal_seconds and flickers until it goes out. Specialists: the Pangolin curls into a scaly ball (scales colors), a flipped Tank lies upside down; the Seal flattens out on a slide with water streaks; the Kraken's tentacles (tentacle) reach out and slam, tentacle_stagger_seconds apart; the Eel's lightning (lightning) jumps from one to the next, crackling the hit before; the Gorilla's shockwave (shock) shakes the field shock_shake; the Red Panda rears up tall (panda ring); the Sloth's slow-motion zone (zone) is drawn on the ground round it, and shots into it take crawl_flight times as long.

army._note: How armies look (Draft Duel). Everyone in a formation marches in step: one walk timing for the whole army, a step every march_stride_tiles of ground it covers, with a thump (stomp_volume_db) and a tiny shake (stomp_shake) on every step; small random differences are kept only for standing about (breathing, fidgets, blinks, expressions). Animals in an army are drawn at squad_scale of their size (so a formation reads as many animals in ranks); an elite Specialist elite_scale bigger; a Mythic hero its hero_scale (classes.json) bigger. Before a fight the armies stand in formation for lineup_seconds, then FIGHT!. The camera frames every animal still standing with camera_margin_tiles around them (and camera_head_room_tiles more above, for their heads and banners) (never closer than camera_min_tiles across or camera_max_zoom), easing over camera_seconds. Squad banners: a flag banner_width x banner_height pixels on a banner_pole pixels pole. Volleys fly slower and higher than single shots (volley_tiles_per_second, between volley_min_seconds and volley_max_seconds, volley_arc times the usual arc). Every other shot in an army fight flies at least over_allies_arc times the usual arc, so it plainly goes over the teammates in between. The clash shakes the field (clash_shake) and freezes it for clash_hitstop_seconds; the War Horn shakes it war_horn_shake. While picking, new squads march in from walk_in_tiles behind the army at walk_in_tiles_per_second (walk_in_steps_per_second steps).

readability._note: Telling who's doing what in a fight. When an animal turns on an enemy biting it up close (the targeting rules' threat response, battle_rules.json "targeting"), a cartoon "!" pops over its head for alert_seconds: alert_size pixels tall, alert_color, popping in with alert_pop overshoot. Not shown for ordinary target changes. Who's shooting at whom: every shot trails a streak in the shooter's team color (blue yours, red the enemy's) over the last shot_trail_seconds of its flight, up to shot_trail_width pixels wide and shot_trail_alpha strong, with a ring of it shot_ring_scale times the shot's size (shot_ring_px wide) round the shot, and its landing sparks take the team color too. The animals' own team bands: "models" team_outline_px (3D) and "characters" team_outline_texels (sprites). Seeing what a squad is doing: a quick tap on its banner (within squad_banner_tap_px) or one of its animals picks it (the same again, or a tap on nothing, lets go; a hold still shows info, and a tool being aimed takes the tap). Its animals glow on the ground (squad_glow_alpha strong, squad_glow_scale times their size, pulsing at squad_pulse_speed) and their 3D band grows squad_band_boost_px wider and brighter; its flag gets a ring; for squad_lines_seconds, dashed lines (squad_line_px wide, squad_dash_px dashes) run from each to the enemy it's going for, with a target ring (squad_marker_px) on that enemy. The fight never pauses or slows for it.

info._note: Holding a card anywhere (picking, offers, army row, deck, bans, collection), or an animal on the battlefield, shows its info popup near the finger (scripts/autoload/hold_info.gd, scripts/ui/info_pop.gd) for as long as it's held; the fight never pauses. hold_seconds: how long a hold takes; move_pixels: moving further than this is a drag (scrolling), not a hold. size: the popup's [width, height] in game pixels; gap: how far it sits from the finger. pop_seconds: its quick pop. The four bars compare the animal with the strongest in the game (at its level): Health and Damage are its whole squad's (on a square-root scale, so everyday animals don't look empty beside a Mythic hero); Speed: speed_bars for each speed; Range: its reach in tiles over range_full_tiles.
